ca_planet_space_ball.blurb: A small bouldering field in the Calavera Hills near Carlsbad, in north San Diego County, sitting just south of the water tower above Calavera Lake. Of its 17 climbs, 16 are boulder problems and one is a top rope. Most problems are easy to moderate, with six at the V0 level and a scattering up to about V4, plus a handful of harder ones reaching into the V6 to V8 range. The setting is scenic and fairly quiet, with views toward the ocean and the preserve, and the low-grade problems make it a friendly first outdoor session. The trails around it are used mostly by mountain bikers, so keep an eye out for them.

ca_dairy_queen_wall_right_side.blurb: The right half of Dairy Queen Wall, a granodiorite face in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park. Nearly all of its 16 routes are traditional, with one top rope, and the rock is split by short, moderate cracks. The grades cluster between 5.6 and 5.8, with a few at 5.9 and 5.10 and a single 5.11 for those wanting more. The base tends to sit in afternoon shade, while the top stays sunny later, especially in summer. It is the busier side of the formation and can get crowded, so expect to share the wall on good weekends.
ca_dairy_queen_wall_right_side.parking_note: Leave the car in the big paved Hemingway lot, the same one used for Hemingway Buttress.
ca_dairy_queen_wall_right_side.approach: From the lot, follow the signed trail toward Hemingway, then cut left toward the wall. The walk is short but finishes with some scrambling up to the base, which can feel awkward for beginners.

ca_negropolis_the.blurb: A cluster of brown granodiorite crags spread across the western side of a bouldery slope near Quail Springs of Joshua Tree National Park, visible from the road. Of its 16 routes, 11 are trad, three are sport and two are top ropes. Grades start around 5.7 and run to 5.11, with most routes falling between 5.9 and 5.11, so this is a spot for climbers already comfortable on intermediate to hard desert lines. The rock is reported as good quality, and the elevated position gives wide views out over the surrounding desert.
ca_negropolis_the.approach: Cross the road and follow a worn path to the dark brown Chocolate Boulders, then scramble up through the boulder field to reach the base of the crag.

ca_short_wall_right_side.blurb: The right-hand portion of the Short Wall in Indian Cove, on the north side of Joshua Tree National Park. It runs from Linda's Crack near the middle of the wall out to its right edge. All 16 routes are trad, and this is the easier and shorter half of the wall: most grades fall between 5.6 and 5.9, with a few easier cracks and one 5.11. It is a pleasant place to log mileage and practice jamming, though none of the lines are standouts. The wall is close to the road, and it can be busy with groups and top-roping parties on weekends.

ca_1_north_face_main.blurb: The main face of Snowshed Wall on Donner Summit, off the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe. Few crags near the summit face due north, and this is one of them, so it stays cool when other walls bake. Fifteen of its 16 routes are traditional and one is sport. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.13, but the bulk fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, making it a place for strong crack and face climbers. The walk from the road takes only a few minutes, and the ledge where many routes begin can get crowded on warm summer days.

ca_billboard_buttress.blurb: A formation right at the entrance of Indian Cove in Joshua Tree National Park, where the road curves around it, so the approach is essentially nothing. It holds 16 climbs: 13 trad lines and three boulder problems. Most grades are modest, running from 5.3 up through 5.10, with one 5.11 and a couple of easy V1 to V2 problems, which makes it a good stop for newer climbers and mixed groups. Faces point south and east, so it is sunny, and like much of Indian Cove it is at its best in the cooler months. Its central spot makes it a common meeting place.

_expect.name: Bavarian Wall and The Far Side

ca_bavarian_wall_and_the_far_side.blurb: A wall in the Scheelite Canyon part of Pine Creek Canyon, above Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. It has 16 routes, nine trad and seven sport, in a fairly steep range of difficulty: one each at 5.8, 5.9 and 5.10, then eight at 5.11 and five at 5.12. That makes it a better pick for confident leaders than for beginners. It gets shade early in the day and warms up later, so it works as a winter sun wall. The crack lines are on good rock, and one multi-pitch tower route is also found here.
